To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 4-hydroxybenzoate/4-hydroxycinnamate degradative pathway gene cluster is linked to the initial dibenzo-p- dioxin pathway genes in Sphingomonasm. sp. strain RW
the genes of an additional degradative pathway are located in the vicinity of the first pathway of the catabolism of dibenzo-p- dioxin and dibenzofuran.

the functional gene cluster for the degradation of 4-hydoxysalicylic acid and hydroxyquinol was identified in Sphingomonasp. strain RW1 and is located immediately downstream of the genes for the initial dioxygenation of dibenzo-p- dioxin and dibenzofuran.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel 4-hydroxybenzoate degradative pathway, which is linked to the initial dibenzo-p -dioxin and dibenzofuran pathways inSphingomons sp. strain RW 1.
the identification of a new catabolic pathway in the bacterium Sphingsomonas sp. RW1.

the elucidation of a new pathway, in which the initial steps of the degradation of dibenzofuran and dibenzo-pdioxin are followed by an oxidative pathway for the degradation of 3-hydrosalicylate and hydroxyquinol.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this gene cluster represents a new type of catabolic gene organization, in which a complete degradative pathway is linked to an initial dioxygenase pathway.
strain RW1 possesses a 3-hydroxysubstituted dibenzofuran/dibenzofuran degradative pathway which is closely linked to a 4-hydroxybenzoate/4-hydroxydiphenyl degradative pathway.
the genes of the initial dio-xygenase pathway are linked to a functional 4-hydroxy-salicylate/hy-droxyquinol degradation pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initial dibenzo-p- dioxin pathway genes in strain RW1 are flanked by the 4-hydroxybenzoyl coenzyme A pathway genes and a functional 4-hydro- xysalicylate pathway gene cluster.

the 4-hydroxybenzoate degradation genes of the RW1 plasmid, pDDB1, are linked to the initial dioxygenases of the dibenzo-p- dioxin and dibenzofuran degradation pathways, whereas the 3-hydroxycinnamate degradation genes are located on the chromosomal region.

the 4-hydroxyphenol/hydroxyquinone degradative genes are located in the same operon as the first dioxygenase genes, and that the 4-HP degradation genes are located between the first two dioxygenase genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the genes for the initial dibenzo-pdioxin dioxygenase system are located on a single plasmid, whereas the genes for the subsequent 4-hydroxy-salicylate and hydroxyquinol degrading pathway are located on the bacterial chromosome.

the 4-hydroxyquinol and 4-hydroxsalicylate pathways are closely linked to the initial dibenzofuran and dibenzo-pdioxin dioxygenase pathways, respectively, and that the genes for the former pathways are organized in a single transcriptional unit.
a complete pathway for the mineralization to carbon dioxide of 4-hy-droxysalicylate and hydroxyquinol (the ketoform of 2-hydroxypenta-2,4-dienoic acid) is encoded by a single gene cluster.
